import sys

def find_pattern(n, m, filenames, indices):
    # Convert indices to 0-based for easier manipulation
    indices = [i - 1 for i in indices]
    
    # Initialize the pattern with '?'
    pattern = ['?'] * len(filenames[0])
    
    # Iterate over each character position
    for pos in range(len(filenames[0])):
        # Get the set of characters at this position for files to be deleted
        chars_to_delete = {filenames[i][pos] for i in indices}
        
        # Get the set of characters at this position for all files
        all_chars = {filename[pos] for filename in filenames}
        
        # If the set of characters to delete is not a subset of all characters,
        # it means we can't create a pattern that matches only the files to be deleted
        if not chars_to_delete.issubset(all_chars):
            return "No"
        
        # If there's more than one character in the set of characters to delete,
        # we can't create a pattern that matches only these files
        if len(chars_to_delete) > 1:
            return "No"
        
        # If there's exactly one character, update the pattern
        if len(chars_to_delete) == 1:
            char = next(iter(chars_to_delete))
            pattern[pos] = char
    
    return "Yes\n" + "".join(pattern)

# Read input
input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()

n = int(data[0])
m = int(data[1])
filenames = data[2:2+n]
indices = list(map(int, data[2+n:]))

# Find and print the pattern
result = find_pattern(n, m, filenames, indices)
print(result)
